trajectory_summary: This call opens with a mismatched expectation (customer thinks a quote was already sent), curdles into open hostility over repeated qualification questions, and ends in a hard capability-based disqualification once the customer reveals he wants a ground-mounted system on five acres. The rep never regains control of tone or pace, and the call closes in under two and a half minutes with no appointment and no bridge attempted before the exit.
outcome_dispute: The correct classification is dq (ground-mount-only property, which Ion's residential-roof-only install model cannot serve), not a soft no_appointment or lost-interest read. The disqualification is structural, not a persuasion failure.

observed_outcome.quote: residential roofs for the home. We can't do ground mounts.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The customer wants a ground-mounted system and Ion only installs on residential roofs; this is a structural capability mismatch that ends the call with no appointment, matching a hard DQ rather than a persuasion failure or soft exit.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captures the $340 figure and simply repeats it back ('Okay. 340.') without connecting it to any pain point or reason to act — the flip should have gone right after the repeat-back, before moving to the roof question.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asks what interested the customer in solar; the call moves directly from intro into address/homeowner verification and never circles back to motivation before the DQ ends the call.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: ground-mount DQ handling and missing schema rule
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I don't want it mounted on my roof. I got five acres. I like it mounted on the ground.
primary_coaching_focus.why: This is the moment that ends the call, and the rep has no scripted or trained path for it — flag to Kenny that this scenario (ground-mount-only property) is a real recurring gap in dq_rules that needs an explicit hard-DQ definition and response script, since reps are currently reacting ad hoc.

key_moments.quote: Oh, I just I'm with the design team. I help, like, get you their design going so we can find out what we can offer you.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep never gives a clean company/role statement matching the script template; instead he improvises after the customer references a quote already sent, leaving the customer's confusion about who is calling unresolved.

key_moments.quote: Black Hills. Those are some of the questions on your fucking questionnaire.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is an overt frustration signal, not a vulnerability disclosure, but the same principle applies: it's a trust-and-tone gift that tells the rep the customer feels re-interrogated. The rep does not acknowledge the frustration at all and moves straight to the next verify item.
The customer gives a clear, specific bill figure. The rep's only response is a flat repeat-back with no emotional flip or acknowledgment of pain.

key_moments.quote: I don't want it mounted on my roof. I got five acres. I like it mounted on the ground.
key_moments.stewart_read: Five acres and an explicit preference for a larger, ground-mounted system signals a highly qualified, high-usage property that would be attractive to install if Ion offered ground mount — this is valuable intel even though it results in a DQ here.
